sections.heading: C — Special driving situations
sections.markdown:
## C — Special driving situations

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A90
Stay alert on quiet rural roads, watch warnings and reduce speed for hazards rather than relaxing attention. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A90
Gravel and dirt provide less grip than concrete or asphalt; slow down and increase following space for longer stops. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A90
Potholes and rippled gravel or dirt surfaces can disturb steering and control. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A90
In dust on gravel roads, use low beams to improve visibility to others, slow down and leave more following room. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A90
Narrow rural roads may have little shoulder and steep nearby ditches; watch narrow-bridge warnings and prepare to stop for opposing traffic. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A90
Slow and increase following room on rural roads with unexpected dips or sharp bends. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A90
Open metal bridge gratings reduce braking and steering grip; slow, hold the wheel firmly and increase following room. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A90
Trees and tall crops can hide traffic near rural corners. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A90
Before a rural hillcrest or sharp curve, slow down, keep to the right and watch for opposing vehicles. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A90
At rural railroad crossings, slow, look both ways and prepare to stop because a crossing may have signs without gates or lights. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A90
Approach uncontrolled rural intersections cautiously at lower speed and be ready to stop for crossing or opposing traffic. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A90
At night, headlights reveal less of the road than daylight, making driving more difficult. [A90]
Source: [A90 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0090]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A91
The handbook recommends dimming high beams about one block before meeting an opposing vehicle. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A91
If an opposing driver uses high beams, a single brief headlight flash may request dimming; if glare continues, look toward the road's right side. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A91
Do not retaliate against high beams by keeping the vehicle's own high beams on. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A91
Use low beams when following another vehicle or driving in heavy traffic, fog, snowfall or heavy rain. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A91
High-beam light reflected by adverse weather can create glare; equipped vehicles may use fog lights in fog, snow or rain. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A91
Avoid staring into approaching headlights because glare can briefly impair vision. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A91
At night, search far ahead for dark shapes and occasionally check both road edges for side hazards. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A91
Do not use sunglasses or tinted glasses at night or on dark days because they reduce useful vision. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A91
Flooding may follow overflowing waterways, failed dams or levees, melting snow runoff or rainfall, and flash floods can develop rapidly. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A91
Do not drive into a flooded road; turn around and choose another route. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A91
Do not attempt a flooded crossing even if it looks shallow because hidden dips or a washed-out roadbed may be present. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A91
If no alternative flood-free route exists, move to higher ground and wait for water to recede. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A91
Work zones may include lane closures, detours or moving equipment and can be temporary or long-term at any season. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A91
Cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles and workers in bright clothing can signal a work zone and guide its traffic. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A91
Orange work-zone signs convey instructions, advance notice and speed information. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A91
Without a reduced work-zone limit, the ordinary posted limit still applies. [A91]
Source: [A91 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0091]

Misconceptions: An empty rural road still has hazards; an apparently shallow flooded road may be washed out; absence of work-zone workers does not cancel signs; swerving around an animal can cause a worse collision.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: surface, sight, space, escape. It organizes hazard checks without adding a driving rule.
Glossary: Distinguish gravel traction, bridge grating, glare, flash flooding, mobile work zones and animal-avoidance control using the source-bound facts.
Dynamic facts: Temporary controls change with roadwork, and weather changes traction and visibility. Edition-bound distances, statistics and unresolved maneuvers require issuer refresh or explicit debt resolution.
